problems: All five binding links rely on in-vitro model predictions rather than direct allele-specific binding or in-vivo occupancy evidence. The predicted direction is consistently ref C greater than alt T, but that does not establish transcriptional or disease effects.
The absence of a cCRE at the variant leaves its regulatory-element status unresolved. PELI2 is only the nearest listed protein-coding gene; no evidence establishes it as the target.
No breast-cancer effect is established by the cited genetic evidence. The low-PIP molecular-QTL result concerns another gene in brain, not a demonstrated breast-cancer mechanism.

For H2, CREB3L4 and CREB3L2 are also expressed, so the family-level prediction does not identify the acting member. E25 and E26 are not-tested results and do not count as evidence against XBP1 or CREB3 binding.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping XBP1 peak in a breast cancer line would strengthen evidence for occupancy in that context; no peak would leave the current prediction unsupported by occupancy data.
A variant-overlapping CREB3 peak in the same breast cancer line could distinguish H2 from H1 on cell-context occupancy.

critique.next_experiment: No change from the existing follow-up priority: perform allele-specific binding validation for the ref and alt alleles, testing the leading candidate TFs (XBP1 and CREB3) separately. If binding is validated, follow with a variant-centered reporter or MPRA assay in a relevant breast cancer cell line and perturb the implicated TF to test whether the effect is TF-dependent.

games.reason: Both chains lack matched ChIP-seq evidence at the variant, so the ChIP evidence does not distinguish them (E25, E26). The binding predictions favor A more directly: the XBP1-mapped model predicts a larger ref-over-alt difference and a much lower alt-allele site-strength percentile than the CREB3-mapped model (E13, E14). XBP1 is also more highly expressed in the stated breast cancer cell-line context, and no XBP1 paralog ambiguity is reported, whereas CREB3L4 and CREB3L2 are listed as unresolved alternatives for B (E13, E14). This is only a relative advantage in computational binding and context evidence; neither chain establishes occupancy, a target gene, or a breast-cancer effect.

Both chains lack matched ChIP-seq support, so occupancy does not distinguish them (E12). XBP1 is more directly supported by the available context: it has higher expression in the breast cancer cell-line context and a larger predicted ref-over-alt binding effect than CREB3 (E13, E14). CREB3 also has expressed paralogs that are not ruled out, adding ambiguity to assigning the binding to CREB3 specifically (E14). These are binding-prediction and expression differences, not evidence of regulatory function or a breast-cancer effect.
